tm_config.hardware: Each Tsetlin Automaton mapped onto the analog conductance of one Y-Flash floating-gate memristor (two transistors, read SR 0.6 um / Vth ~0.3 V and injection SI 0.3 um / Vth ~1.5 V, shared drain and floating gate, commercial 180 nm CMOS, two-terminal mode with sources shorted, self-selecting, no selector). An accumulating divergence counter sums TA state changes over training points and issues a blind program/erase pulse (0.5 ms width in this experiment) when it crosses +-15, then resets. Simulated with a compact Y-Flash model including D2D and C2C variation [14]. 8 TAs shown, 5000 training points, 2N = 300 TA states (decision boundary 150); 19 pulses to track the trajectories; max included TA 2.33 uS, min excluded TA 23.2 nS.

notes: Device/mapping study: no accuracy, latency or throughput. Table II reports a single Y-Flash device's average power and energy per pulse (read 2 V/40 states, program 5 V/40 states, erase 8 V/32 states); results 1-3 are device-level (tm_config null). It is not clear whether the Table II and C2C/D2D numbers are measurements on fabricated devices or come from the compact model of [14]: Sec. II says a compact model is used, Sec. III says 'we performed the cycling performance test'. Inconsistency in the paper: Fig. 6 caption says LCS/HCS distributions over 100 cycles while the text says 250 cycles; the record follows the text. Erase states in Table II are 32 although the text speaks of 40 states for both modes. Whether the XOR dataset is the noisy XOR variant is not stated.
